parts.name: Serosa
parts.description: Serosa (visceral peritoneum): a simple squamous mesothelium on a thin layer of loose connective tissue carrying vessels, lymphatics and fat. Its secretions let the loops slide freely. The retroperitoneal parts of the gut (most of the duodenum, ascending and descending colon) have an adventitia instead on their posterior surface.

parts.name: Outer longitudinal muscle
parts.description: Outer longitudinal layer of the muscularis externa: smooth muscle bundles running along the gut. Contraction shortens the segment; coordinated with the circular layer by the myenteric plexus it produces peristalsis and segmentation. Continuous representative muscle stratum with fitted myenteric nerve recesses; the surface ridges indicate fibre direction schematically.

parts.name: Inner circular muscle
parts.description: Inner circular layer of the muscularis externa: bundles wrapped around the gut. Contraction narrows the lumen; the layer thickens to form the pyloric, ileocaecal and internal anal sphincters. The interstitial cells of Cajal (pacemakers of the slow waves) lie at its borders. Continuous representative circular stratum with fitted myenteric nerve recesses; the surface ridges indicate fibre direction schematically.

parts.name: Submucosa
parts.description: Submucosa: dense irregular connective tissue carrying the larger arterioles, venules, lymphatics and the submucosal plexus. It gives the wall its strength - it is the layer that holds sutures.

parts.name: Muscularis mucosae
parts.description: Muscularis mucosae: a thin layer of smooth muscle (inner circular, outer longitudinal) at the base of the mucosa. It moves the mucosa locally, independently of peristalsis. In colorectal cancer, invasion through it into the submucosa is what defines an invasive carcinoma (pT1).

parts.name: Myenteric (Auerbach) plexus
parts.description: Myenteric (Auerbach) plexus: ganglia and interconnecting nerve strands between the circular and longitudinal muscle layers. Part of the enteric nervous system, it controls motility (peristalsis) and is modulated by vagal and sympathetic input. Ganglion cells are absent in Hirschsprung disease and lost in achalasia and Chagas disease.

parts.name: Submucosal (Meissner) plexus
parts.description: Submucosal (Meissner) plexus: small ganglia and nerve strands in the submucosa next to the muscularis mucosae. It controls epithelial secretion, absorption and local blood flow and the muscularis mucosae. In Hirschsprung disease its ganglion cells are absent too - a suction rectal biopsy, which samples the submucosa, is diagnostic.

parts.name: Submucosal arterioles
parts.description: Submucosal arterioles: branches of the vasa recta forming a submucosal plexus, from which arterioles pierce the muscularis mucosae to supply the crypts and the villus capillary loops.

parts.name: Submucosal venules
parts.description: Submucosal venules: collect blood from the mucosa. Intestinal venous blood, rich in absorbed sugars and amino acids, drains through the superior and inferior mesenteric veins into the hepatic portal vein.

parts.name: Mucosal branches
parts.description: Mucosal branches: small arterioles and venules crossing the muscularis mucosae between the submucosal plexus and the capillaries of the lamina propria and villi.

parts.name: Submucosal lymphatic collectors
parts.description: Representative submucosal collectors receive the displayed lacteal necks through actual wall ports. Their open lateral ends are specimen crop handoffs; the remaining lymphatic plexus is outside this tissue window.

parts.name: Lamina propria
parts.description: Lamina propria: loose (areolar) connective tissue between the crypts, rich in IgA-secreting plasma cells, lymphocytes, macrophages, eosinophils, fenestrated capillaries and lymphatics - the diffuse part of the gut-associated lymphoid tissue (GALT).

parts.name: Villus lamina propria core
parts.description: Continuous villus lamina propria fitted immediately beneath actual basal epithelial envelopes, with original blood, lymph and smooth-muscle recesses retained. No natural empty annular compartment is implied.

parts.name: Central lacteals
parts.description: Central lacteal: a blind-ended lymphatic capillary in the axis of each villus. It takes up chylomicrons (absorbed dietary fat), which are too large to enter blood capillaries, and carries them via mesenteric lymphatics and the cisterna chyli to the thoracic duct - lymph (chyle) is milky after a fatty meal.

parts.name: Villus capillary network
parts.description: Villus capillary network: an arteriole ascends the villus and breaks up at the tip into a fenestrated capillary net lying just beneath the epithelium, drained by a venule. It absorbs water-soluble nutrients (monosaccharides, amino acids) into the portal circulation. The countercurrent arrangement makes the villus tip relatively hypoxic, so it is the first part injured in ischaemia.

parts.name: Villus smooth muscle
parts.description: Villus smooth muscle: strands from the muscularis mucosae running up the villus core beside the lacteal. Their rhythmic contraction shortens the villus and pumps chyle out of the lacteal.

parts.name: Peyer patch follicles
